title: dynamic-token-window-scheduler-with-kv-pinning-and-soft-timeouts
author: Priya Nambiar
description: Motivation: continuous-batcher tail latency and starvation for KV-heavy requests observed under mixed workloads. This PR implements a dynamic token-window scheduler that adapts per-queue token windows based on observed per-request token latency distribution and active KV cache pressure. Key changes: 1) token-window autosize: scheduler observes amortized tokens-per-millisecond per-client and expands or contracts the per-dequeue token window to hit target p95 token latency; 2) soft-timeouts: introduce a soft timeout layer that signals graceful preemption (reduce slice size) before hard deadline cancel to preserve fairness without excessive aborts; 3) KV-pinning heuristics: requests that hit the KV cache with high reuse are given transient pin tokens to reduce re-warm churn, with a decay counter to prevent long-term starvation; 4) starvation detector: lightweight per-queue aging counter that escalates priority for queues that have been bypassed beyond a threshold; 5) kernel-hints: expose an opt-in hint to the kernel selector that prioritizes single-token micro-kernel for sub-slice continuations to reduce overhead on short tails; 6) telemetry: add new metrics (scheduler.window_size, scheduler.soft_timeouts_triggered, kv.pin_hits/evictions) and dashboard panels; 7) safety and rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag scheduler.token_window_compensator with default disabled, canary rollout plan included. Implementation notes: most logic is in a new scheduler component with careful locking to avoid hot-path allocations; KV pin uses a compact decay counter to limit memory. Tests and validation: unit tests for resizing logic and starvation escalation; deterministic simulation harness exercising mixed KV/cache miss patterns; perf lab runs showing 6-9% improvement in 99th-token-latency on our standard continuous-batching benchmark with KV-heavy mix, and median token cost unchanged. Checklist: ensure canary gate is toggled via console; validate metrics emission in canary; coordinate rollout with infra to monitor tail latency dashboards; add a short-term kill switch for immediate rollback; update release notes and ops runbook; link to Linear tickets. Why different from previous work: this PR focuses on adaptive per-queue token windows and explicit KV pin decay to address repeated KV re-warm induced starvation rather than purely queue-slot rebalancing. Risks and mitigations: mis-sized windows can oscillate so we use slow Euler-style smoothing and min/max bounds; KV-pins could starve low-reuse clients, mitigated by decay counters and starvation escalation. Rollout plan: 0% -> 5% canary -> 25% -> 100% with checks at each step. See commits_summary and CI results for details.

feat: dynamic window resizing with EWMA smoothing
feat: soft-timeout preemption and slice reduction logic
feat: kv pin manager and decay counters
perf: kernel hint plumbing and micro-kernel preference flag
test: deterministic harness + unit tests for escalation and resizing

changed_file_snippets: token_window_scheduler.cpp: added resize loop with EWMA smoothing and bounds checks; critical path avoids allocations by reusing deque buffers
kv_pin_manager.go: compact decay counter (uint8) per-client, eviction logic when global pin budget exceeded
soft_timeout_policy.cpp: injects soft timeout signal before hard deadline and requests slice reduction instead of immediate cancel
review_comments: Evan Li: Could you add a microbenchmark that isolates the EWMA smoothing parameters? We need to justify chosen tau and min/max bounds for production. Author: added token_window_simulation_test.cc with parameter sweep and included recommendations in comments.

Diego Morales: Concerned about KV-pin memory pressure on large tenant counts. Suggest limiting total pin budget per-node and enforcing LRU on weakly-referenced pins. Author: implemented global pin budget and LRU eviction as fallback; documented limits in runtime_flags.yaml.

Aisha Khan: Can soft-timeout churn increase overall compute if slices shrink too aggressively? Request telemetry for slice shrink/grow events. Author: added metrics scheduler.soft_timeouts_triggered and scheduler.slice_adjustments, and included them in dashboard panels.
Infra (automated): canary gate added to runtime flags and console feature flag; confirm orchestration will respect runtime restart semantics.
QA: found intermittent flake in kv_pin_decay_test.go on low-memory CI shards; increased memory headroom in test harness and reran.
Evan Li: Approved after reviewing perf bench runs and simulation outputs. Diego Morales: Approved with nit on docs wording. Aisha Khan: Approved.

release_notes: Adaptive token-window scheduler with KV pinning and soft timeouts to reduce continuous-batcher tail latency and prevent KV-induced starvation. Feature gated behind scheduler.token_window_compensator. Expect ~6-9% 99th-token-latency improvement in KV-heavy workloads. See ops runbook for rollout steps.
